name: Ameren Corporation
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated electric and natural-gas franchises in Missouri and Illinois (Ameren Missouri, Ameren Illinois) plus FERC-regulated transmission, with essential inelastic demand and a $31.8B infrastructure plan guided to ~10.6% rate-base CAGR through 2030 and 2.8 GW of signed large-load agreements — a durable, visible compounding machine. Capped at 6 because regulators (MoPSC, ICC, FERC) set the allowed return so there is no pricing power beyond rate cases, Illinois recovery is capped / more restrictive, the plan is funded with debt (net debt $19,174M) plus recurring equity issuance (share count +1.61%/yr), and coal-retirement and gas-transition costs sit with the equity if recovery is denied.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: Durable MO/IL regulated monopoly, moat 6/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in all of the last 5 years and on TTM (capex exceeds OCF; normalized base -$4.02/share, TTM -$5.13/share) — Tier F on this screen; guided 6-8% EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
moat_for: Exclusive regulated electric and gas franchises in Missouri and Illinois — captive, essential-service customers
$31.8B regulated infrastructure plan guided to ~10.6% rate-base CAGR 2025-2030, largely recovered through rates / riders
FERC-regulated transmission (Ameren Transmission / ATXI, MISO long-range projects) earns formula-rate returns
2.8 GW of signed large-load electric service agreements by 2030 under an approved Missouri large-load rate plan
moat_against: Regulators cap returns — MoPSC, ICC and FERC set allowed ROE and recovery; no pricing power beyond rate cases
Illinois is the tougher jurisdiction: MYRP reconciliation cap and ICC restrictiveness create disallowance / lag risk
Growth is debt- plus equity-funded: net debt $19,174M and share count +1.61%/yr dilutes rate-base growth per share
Coal retirement / Rush Island remediation and gas-network transition risk; large-load data-center demand could face recovery pushback
